nodes.name: Ru@Mn₃O₄ Hybrid Hydrogel Formation
nodes.procedure: The Ru@Mn₃O₄ hybrid hydrogel blocks were synthesized via a simple wet-chemical process, with a post-treatment at 60°C for 12 h. Finally, Ru@Mn₃O₄ was obtained by freeze-drying method.

nodes.source_text: The Ru@Mn₃O₄ hybrid hydrogel blocks were synthesized via a simple wet-chemical process, with a post-treatment at 60°C for 12 h. Finally, Ru@Mn₃O₄ was obtained by freeze-drying method (Figure S1)

Tafel slope of 30 mV dec⁻¹... MA of 23.5 A mg⁻¹... C_dl of 27.5 mF cm⁻² and ECSA of 171.8 cm²... TOF of 8.5 H₂ s⁻¹... overpotential at 10 mA cm⁻² only has 1 mV attenuation after 5000 CV cycles... attenuates only 1% in 40 h

nodes.characterization_summary: Morphology of Ru@Mn₃O₄ similar to pure Mn₃O₄ with ultrafine Ru clusters decorated on support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of Ru@Mn₃O₄ is similar with the pure Mn₃O₄ (Figures 1a and S2).

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes show 0.22 nm for Ru(002) and 0.26 nm for Mn₃O₄(103) with lattice contraction from 0.27 nm in pure Mn₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The measured lattice spacing (0.22 nm) matches well with the (002) facet of Ru... The interplanar spacing of 0.26 nm is assigned to the (103) crystal plane of Mn₃O₄, which is smaller than... pure Mn₃O₄ (0.27 nm).

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of O, Mn, and Ru elements confirmed in Ru@Mn₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark field-scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image and EDS mapping of Ru@Mn₃O₄ (Figure 1d) indicate the uniform distributions of O, Mn, and Ru elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform elemental mapping of Ru, Mn, O in the heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM image and EDS mapping of Ru@Mn₃O₄ (Figure 1d) indicate the uniform distributions of O, Mn, and Ru elements in Ru@Mn₃O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: Only Mn₃O₄ diffraction peaks observed (JCPDS: 24-0734) with peak shift to higher angles and widened half-peak widths indicating lattice shrinkage and amorphous phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By comparing the XRD patterns of Ru@Mn₃O₄, Mn₃O₄, and Ru/Mn₃O₄, there are only diffraction signals of Mn₃O₄ for the Ru@Mn₃O₄ composite (JCPDS: 24-0734)... the characteristic XRD peaks of Ru@Mn₃O₄ shift to higher angles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content in Ru@Mn₃O₄ is 7.2 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma (ICPMS) measurements confirm that Ru content in Ru@Mn₃O₄ is only 7.2 wt% (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p peaks shift +0.5 eV in Ru@Mn₃O₄ vs Ru NPs; new Ru-O peaks at 465.2/487.7 eV; O 1s new peak at 529.8 eV for Ru-O-Mn; Mn 3p shifts -0.19 eV indicating electron transfer Ru→Mn₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to Ru NPs and Ru/Mn₃O₄, the binding energy from Ru@Mn₃O₄ presents a positive shift of 0.5 eV... two new peaks at 465.2 and 487.7 eV... ascribed to the Ru-O bond... a new peak at 529.8 eV... interfacial Ru-O-Mn bonds... Mn 3p XPS spectra with the negative shift of about 0.19 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows electron transfer from Ru to Mn₃O₄; FT-EXAFS reveals dominant Ru-Ru coordination at 2.68 Å and Ru-O-Mn at 2.02 Å; Mn K-edge shows Mn-O-Mn/Ru at 3.20 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1g shows electron transfer from Ru to Mn₃O₄... The extended X-ray adsorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra (Figure 1h) show that Mn₃O₄ holds a dominant Ru-Ru coordination (2.68 Å) and minor Ru-O-Mn coordination (2.02 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: New peak at 503.6 cm⁻¹ confirms Ru-O-Mn bonds formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This point is also confirmed by Raman spectroscopy with the newly emerged peak at 503.6 cm⁻¹ in Ru@Mn₃O₄ (Figure S11b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl = 27.5 mF cm⁻² yielding ECSA = 171.8 cm² for Ru@Mn₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl and ECSA values of Ru@Mn₃O₄ are 27.5 mF cm⁻² and 171.8 cm², respectively (Figures 2f and S20).
